hints.title: Zero Compaction Order Preservation Obstacle
hints.text: Removing zeroes individually incurs quadratic element shifting and copying into a temporary list violates the in-place constraint. How can you shift non-zero values forward while keeping their relative order intact?

hints.title: Non-Zero Insertion Pointer
hints.text: Maintain an insertion index for non-zero elements. Whenever a non-zero value is encountered during traversal, swap it with the element at the insertion pointer and advance the pointer.

hints.title: In-Place Partition Procedure
hints.text: Set insert_idx to zero. Loop index i through the array. When nums[i] is not zero, swap nums[insert_idx] and nums[i], then increment insert_idx. Every swap pushes non-zero elements forward and accumulates zeroes behind.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of nums array (1 <= N <= 10^4)
complexity.notes: Single pass swap compaction preserving relative order with O(1) space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Filtering into a separate list and copying back requires O(N) auxiliary space, violating the in-place modification requirement.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Swapping non-zero items into the write boundary achieves O(N) time without secondary arrays.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Minimizing the total number of write operations when the array has few or zero zeroes.
